subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should main-session `systemEvent` cron jobs support provider/model overrides through `payload.model`, top-level cron fields, or an explicit `sessionOverride` block, and should invalid models fail closed or use existing fallback behavior?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API shape affects cron protocol compatibility, session state ownership, provider/auth routing, and upgrade semantics.

options.title: Add explicit sessionOverride block
options.body: Create a typed provider/model override block for main-session systemEvent jobs, with validation and tests for wake-now and next-heartbeat paths.

options.title: Reuse payload.model
options.body: Extend the existing agentTurn model field onto systemEvent payloads for parity, but require direct typed propagation instead of context-key encoding.

options.title: Keep systemEvent tied to session state
options.body: Document dedicated cron session keys plus session model selection as the supported workaround and leave job-level overrides unsupported.

recommendation.title: Add explicit sessionOverride block
recommendation.body: Create a typed provider/model override block for main-session systemEvent jobs, with validation and tests for wake-now and next-heartbeat paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the clearest recent maintainer context from the adjacent cron model UI landing and its explicit systemEvent scoping decision.
